clue.text: Bore with a comforting message?

parts.note: a bore is a shaft sunk for water, and one that answers your hopes would carry a comforting message: the coin-in-the-water kind of shaft

explanation.surface: A tedious person who at least has something reassuring to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' wants to be a dull person; it is a shaft drilled for water, and the 'comforting message' is the granting of a wish.
explanation.definitionFit: A wishing well is a water shaft into which people toss coins hoping their wishes come true.

clue.text: Sounds like a Cockney greeting, he observes

indicators.note: the clue says the next words, when spoken, resemble the word wanted

parts.note: wotcher is the Cockney (East London) slang hello, from 'what cheer'

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdrops on a Londoner saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: Wotcher is a London working-class greeting; said aloud it matches the word for an onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker or observer is a person who watches.

clue.text: Condition leaving one at a loss for words

definitions.text: Condition leaving one at a loss for words

parts.words: Condition leaving one at a loss for words
parts.note: describes the state of being so stunned that no words come out

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding state that leaves someone unable to find anything to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dumbstruck, unable to utter anything, is this state.

clue.text: One admired with only 50 cents

annotationWithheld.why: One admired with only 50 cents (4): IDOL is I + DOL (half of DOLLAR), but 'One' must give I and also begin the definition 'One admired'; no reading leaves each word one job.

clue.text: Where key troops gather in Hampshire

definitions.text: Where key troops gather in Hampshire

parts.note: G is a musical key

indicators.note: the troops collect into a new formation, so their letters are regrouped

explanation.surface: A Hampshire town where soldiers assemble at a key point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gather' rearranges TROOPS into OSPORT after G. Gosport is a naval town on the Hampshire coast in southern England, opposite Portsmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosport is a harbour town in the English county of Hampshire with long military ties.

clue.text: See 1
Use pure wit in a report

indicators.note: to use the letters is to put them to work in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Advice to a journalist to employ clean humour in an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' is the anagram signal: PUREWIT is reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: A write-up is a newspaper account or review of an event.

clue.text: Close fast with a Rugby player

definitions.meaning: to secure a door shut with a key

explanation.surface: Shutting things firmly with the help of a rugby forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten shut with a bolt is one sense; a second-row forward in a rugby scrum is the other.

clue.text: Moral deterrent carrying little weight

definitions.meaning: a qualm of conscience that holds one back
an old apothecaries' unit of twenty grains

explanation.surface: A conscience that weighs almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualm that stops wrongdoing is one sense; an old apothecaries' measure of twenty grains is the other.

clue.text: Strength displayed by non-meat eaters?

parts.note: playfully treats the moral fibre of vegetarians as plant-based tissue

explanation.surface: The robustness shown by vegetarians.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant tissue such as cotton or jute strands is called this; the clue pretends it is the grit of herbivores.

clue.text: Land ahoy, it's plain to see

definitions.text: Land ahoy, it's plain to see

parts.words: Land ahoy, it's plain to see
parts.note: a lookout crying that the shoreline is plainly visible, punning on the idiom for no danger in sight

explanation.surface: A sailor spots the shore clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means nobody is watching, so it is safe to proceed; literally the shoreline is in plain view.

clue.text: Drink to have with the joint

definitions.meaning: a German white wine from the Rhine
the ankle joint in a horse's hind leg

explanation.surface: Advice on which wine goes with the Sunday roast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhine white wine is one sense; the hind-leg ankle joint of a horse is the other.

clue.text: He's got the message, it's understood

explanation.surface: A listener confirms the message is clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators say this word to confirm a transmission was received and understood.

clue.text: Show emotion as we get the record

parts.note: taken as written
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Getting tearful on receiving a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying is the standard way to show strong feeling.

clue.text: Used by the Chancellor to balance the Budget with tonic effect

definitions.text: Used by the Chancellor to balance the Budget with tonic effect

parts.words: Used by the Chancellor to balance the Budget with tonic effect
parts.note: John ... was Chancellor of the Exchequer, a balance is a weighing device, and a tonic is the keynote of a musical series of notes

explanation.surface: A Treasury minister's tool for making the national accounts add up and feel healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: John Major was the UK's Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) in 1989-90; a 'Major scale' would be his weighing balance.
explanation.definitionFit: A major scale is the eight-note sequence built up from its tonic, the home note of a key.

clue.text: See 13
Trustworthy teacher of Samuel in storm

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to rant is to storm angrily
Eli was the priest who brought up the boy Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A dependable biblical tutor caught up in a tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone trustworthy is dependable and can be counted on.

clue.text: Choose a weapon, albeit there's no choice

definitions.text: Choose a weapon, albeit there's no choice

parts.words: Choose a weapon, albeit there's no choice
parts.note: joins a word for choose with a chopping weapon, then jokes that the result is a pick offering no option

explanation.surface: A duellist told to select arms when only one is on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A digging tool with a pointed head; its name joins a word for select with a word for a chopper.

clue.text: The material sets our fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape something anew, so these letters are remade

explanation.surface: A fabric that dictates the style of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' is a verb here, rearranging SETSOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussore is a coarse wild silk fabric from India.

clue.text: A measure moved by top Wets

indicators.note: the letters shift position into a new order

explanation.surface: A policy shifted by senior Tory moderates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wets' were moderate Conservatives under Margaret Thatcher; 'measure' is an old word for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure in the old sense is a dance, and this is a ballroom dance in duple time.

clue.text: Ornamental dish of green peas as an exception

indicators.note: the letters of the second word are excepted, taken out of the shuffled first phrase

explanation.surface: A fancy serving bowl holding garden produce.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging GREENPEAS gives the answer plus A and S, which 'an exception' sets aside.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is a decorative centrepiece for a dining table, often with branching dishes.

clue.text: A church porch from the biblical town

definitions.meaning: a chapel or porch at the west end of some churches
the region of northern Palestine where much of the Gospel story is set

explanation.surface: An entrance taken from a place in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A porch at the west end of a church is one sense; the New Testament region by its lake is the other.

clue.text: Well-delineated form of art

definitions.meaning: art based on drawing and printing

explanation.surface: A clearly outlined artistic style.
explanation.definitionFit: Vividly clear is one sense; the visual arts of drawing and printmaking are the other.

clue.text: Made certain in the finish

definitions.note: made in the sense of caused something to happen

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the end is the finish
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Something was guaranteed at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something happen is to guarantee it will occur.

clue.text: Alternative direction in Normandy

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
NE is northeast, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Another route through northern France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orne is a river and département in Normandy, northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orne is a river and administrative department of Normandy.

clue.text: To write a letter can be punishing

parts.note: to pen is to write
L is a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Writing a single letter can be a painful chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal means relating to punishment.

clue.text: Creatures with small feet pointed at both ends

indicators.note: the points sit on either side, bracketing the other piece

parts.note: E and S are compass points
ft is the short form of feet

explanation.surface: Animals with tiny, sharp-tipped feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Efts are young newts, small amphibians.

clue.text: Time that is right for a row

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: The right moment for a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is a line of seats, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one level in a series of rows, as in a stadium.

clue.text: Boat with business between two points

indicators.note: the second piece sits between the two letters of the first

parts.note: S and W are compass points
co is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A vessel used for trade between two places.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed barge.

clue.text: Up the pole in Scotland!

parts.note: up the pole is slang for crazy, but here the pole is a tree trunk heaved into the air at Highland games

explanation.surface: A Scot is said to have gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: At Highland games in Scotland, athletes heave a long wooden pole so it flips end over end.
explanation.definitionFit: This Highland games event involves flinging a heavy wooden pole so it turns over.

clue.text: Forecast for fish

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, scattering these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A weather prediction for anglers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forecast' must be split: FORE is the fodder and 'cast' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe is a freshwater fish of the carp family, also called the ide.

clue.text: Neat occupation

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so this is a job tending them

explanation.surface: A tidy line of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowherd's job is looking after cattle, which old English called neat.
